paragraphs: Friend, this chapter is a LOT of names. Chiefs, kings, grandsons, more chiefs. But here's what it's telling us: Esau's family was real, and it grew into a whole nation. The chapter ends with "Esau was the father of the Edomites." (Genesis 36:43)

Look at the moment Esau moves. His possessions were "too great for them to dwell together," so he settled in the area of Mount Seir. (Genesis 36:7-8) Now Esau had a whole nation come out of him, and the Bible writes down his sons, grandsons, chiefs and kings by name. I think that's a quiet reminder that no person is a throwaway to God, even the ones who aren't the main character of the book.

So here's the big idea, baker. When you hit a long list of names in your Bible, don't skim it like the terms and conditions on your phone. Somebody put every one of those names there on purpose, and they tell us the Bible is about real people in real places. Slow down, say a few of them out loud, and be glad that a God who keeps track of all these names keeps track of you too.
